brief.headline: Force Opus to prove its work before it calls a task done
brief.summary:
Two repos this cycle (fablize, fable-method) take the completion/evidence/verification discipline that made Claude Fable reliable and package it as something installable on Opus or any subagent tonight — think/act/prove as a hard gate instead of trusting the model's own summary. Pair that with David Crawshaw's nightly cron prompt (pull upstream, rebase local changes, verify, swap in the new build) as a working template for the actual sleep-then-review loop, and ponytail's "laziest senior dev" skill set to keep the diffs small enough to review in the morning instead of wading through overengineered output.

On cost, a cluster of proxy and control-plane repos (opencodex, claudexor, omnigent, claude-dynamic-workflows-codex) let you keep Claude Code as the front end while routing individual subagent calls to local Ollama, DeepSeek, or a cheaper Codex backend — worth trialing on your lowest-stakes calls like lint fixes or commit messages before trusting anything bigger to them. AirLLM's 4GB-GPU 70B trick and dao-code's DeepSeek-V4 cache-prefix engineering point the same direction: real hardware-bound savings, not leaderboard talk. And the SQLite tracker getting flooded with plausible-but-fake AI-generated vulnerability reports is the failure report to actually heed — anything your agent writes up as a "finding" needs a repro script or failing test attached before it counts as verified.
bullets: Install fivetaku/fablize as a Claude Code plugin to force Opus through completion/evidence/verification before it marks anything done
Cron David Crawshaw's nightly prompt — pull upstream, rebase, verify, swap in — as a template for the sleep-then-review loop
Clone Sahir619/fable-method and wire its think/act/prove eval as a hard completion gate on your subagents
Load DietrichGebert/ponytail's skill set to keep overnight diffs small and actually reviewable
Route lint/commit-message subagent calls through lidge-jun/opencodex to a local Ollama or DeepSeek model to cut API spend
Require a repro script or failing test before accepting any agent-authored bug or security finding — SQLite's tracker is drowning in plausible fake CVEs

items.title: fivetaku/fablize — A Claude Code plugin that makes Opus behave like Fable — completion, evidence, and verification enforced as procedure. Ships only what a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved transferable.
items.tldr: Claude Code plugin fablize forces Opus through the same completion/evidence/verification procedure that made Fable reliable, keeping only what testing proved transferable.
items.whyItMatters: An installable enforcement layer that makes Opus verify its own work before declaring a task done — exactly the unattended-then-review workflow you want.
items.tryThis: Install fivetaku/fablize as a Claude Code plugin and point it at your Opus subagents.

items.title: Quoting David Crawshaw's prompt
items.tldr: David Crawshaw runs a nightly cron job whose prompt tells an agent to pull upstream changes, rebase local modifications on top, verify the software still works, and swap in the new build.
items.whyItMatters: It's a ready template for the exact unattended 'describe it, sleep, review a working result' loop, applied to keeping a fork or vendored tool current.
items.tryThis: Cron a nightly prompt: 'fetch upstream changes to <software>, rebase local changes on top, verify it still works, then replace the current version.'

items.title: DietrichGebert/ponytail — Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.tldr: Ponytail, a viral (94.8k-star) prompt/skill framework, pushes agents toward a 'laziest senior dev' instinct — write the least code possible instead of over-engineering.
items.whyItMatters: A drop-in prompting discipline to curb the bloated, hard-to-review diffs agents tend to produce on long unattended runs.
items.tryThis: Clone DietrichGebert/ponytail and load its skill/prompt set into your Claude Code config.

items.title: cobusgreyling/loop-engineering — Practical patterns, starters & CLI tools for loop engineering with AI coding agents. Design systems that prompt and orchestrate agents (inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny). Includes loop-audit, loop-in
items.tldr: loop-engineering packages CLI tools (loop-audit, loop-init, loop-cost) and starter patterns for designing and orchestrating unattended AI coding-agent loops, inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you concrete commands to scaffold, audit, and cost-track long-running agent loops instead of hand-rolling your own harness around Claude Code.
items.tryThis: Clone cobusgreyling/loop-engineering, run loop-init to scaffold a loop, then loop-audit against one of your existing agent workflows.

items.title: omnigent-ai/omnigent — Omnigent is an open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness: orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents — swap harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in rea
items.tldr: Omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Pi agents interchangeably, with policy enforcement, sandboxing, and control from any device.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you one control plane to swap or mix harnesses and to check on or steer an overnight run remotely instead of being tied to your desk.
items.tryThis: Clone omnigent-ai/omnigent and wire an existing worktree workflow through it to test steering a run from your phone.

items.title: lidge-jun/opencodex — Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code — use any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama…) with Codex CLI, App, SDK, and Claude Code
items.tldr: opencodex is a proxy that lets Codex CLI/App/SDK and Claude Code call any LLM — Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, or a local Ollama model.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you route cheap or low-stakes subagent calls to a local/cheaper model without abandoning your existing Codex or Claude Code setup.
items.tryThis: Clone lidge-jun/opencodex and route a low-stakes subagent (lint fixes, commit messages) through it to a local Ollama model.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: A GitHub repo distills the Fable agent workflow into reusable skills plus an eval harness enforcing think/act/prove before work is marked done.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a portable verification loop you can bolt onto any subagent so it has to prove its work before you see the PR, not just trust its own summary.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method and wire its eval as a completion gate in your subagent pipeline.

items.title: tigicion/dao-code — Open-source TypeScript terminal coding agent for DeepSeek-V4 — builds on DeepSeek's strong price-performance and ultra-cheap cache pricing, engineering byte-stable prefixes and cache-reusing forks so cross-session memory
items.tldr: dao-code is a terminal coding agent built around DeepSeek-V4, engineered with byte-stable prompt prefixes and cache-reusing forks to make cross-session memory nearly free.
items.whyItMatters: If you're paying per token, DeepSeek-V4's cache pricing plus this repo's prefix engineering can meaningfully cut the cost of long unattended sessions, and it's Claude Code config compatible (Skills/MCP/Hooks).
items.tryThis: Clone tigicion/dao-code and use it as the backend for one long-context subagent to check actual cache-hit cost savings.

items.title: CodeBendKit/codeseek — Rust-powered code intelligence CLI for AI coding agents. Builds call graphs and hybrid semantic search indexes (Dense + Sparse + RRF + Reranker) across 7 languages. Ships as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex
items.tldr: codeseek is a Rust CLI that builds call graphs and hybrid dense+sparse+reranked semantic search indexes across 7 languages, exposed as MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex CLI.
items.whyItMatters: Better code retrieval means fewer clarifying questions and less back-and-forth for an agent working a large codebase — directly extends how long it can run unattended.
items.tryThis: Add CodeBendKit/codeseek as an MCP server in your Claude Code config so subagents get call-graph search instead of grep.

items.title: razzant/claudexor — Multi-harness control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode: quota-aware rotation across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions, shared thread context, and cross-model review.
items.tldr: claudexor is a control plane that rotates across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions by quota, shares thread context, and runs cross-model review on outputs.
items.whyItMatters: Cross-model review gives you a second model checking your agent's work before a PR reaches you, and quota rotation avoids getting rate-limited mid-run.
items.tryThis: Set up razzant/claudexor and route your overnight run's final review step to a different model than the one that wrote the code.

items.title: scasella/claude-dynamic-workflows-codex — Run Claude Code dynamic workflows on a local Codex (GPT) backend, plus an interactive run viewer
items.tldr: This repo runs Claude Code's dynamic workflow feature against a local Codex/GPT backend, plus an interactive viewer for inspecting runs.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you keep your existing Workflow scripts while swapping a local or cheaper backend into some pipeline stages, and the run viewer helps you audit what an unattended run actually did.
items.tryThis: Clone scasella/claude-dynamic-workflows-codex and point one pipeline stage at a local Codex backend to compare cost against Claude Code proper.

items.title: AirLLM 70B inference with single 4GB GPU
items.tldr: AirLLM runs 70B-parameter inference on a single 4GB GPU by streaming layers instead of loading the whole model into memory.
items.whyItMatters: Puts a 70B-class model within reach of a modest local GPU for offline or low-priority subagent work instead of paying API rates.
items.tryThis: Try AirLLM on your existing 4GB+ GPU for a low-priority subagent task like commit-message drafting or lint triage.

items.title: SQLite Critical CVEs or LLM Slop?
items.tldr: AI-generated vulnerability reports are reportedly flooding SQLite's bug tracker with plausible-looking but fake CVEs.
items.whyItMatters: A live example of agent output that looks reviewable but isn't — the same failure mode that can hide inside an unattended agent's PR if claims aren't checked against an actual repro.
items.tryThis: Require a repro script or failing test as a hard gate before any agent-authored bug or security report leaves draft.

items.title: oomol-lab/open-connector — Open-source auth gateway connecting 1000+ SaaS providers to AI agents through SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.tldr: Open-connector is an open-source auth gateway exposing 1000+ SaaS providers to AI agents through one SDK/CLI/MCP/HTTP/OpenAPI interface.
items.whyItMatters: Collapses the per-service boilerplate of wiring new SaaS accounts into your agents' MCP tool list into a single gateway.
items.tryThis: Clone oomol-lab/open-connector and register it as an MCP server for the SaaS accounts your agents need.

items.title: gi-dellav/zerostack — Lightweight coding agent written in Rust, optimized for memory footprint and performance
items.tldr: zerostack is a new lightweight coding agent written in Rust, built specifically to minimize memory footprint.
items.whyItMatters: A leaner agent runtime could let you run more parallel subagents per machine or on smaller hardware than Electron/Node-based agents, cutting the resource cost of unattended overnight runs.
items.tryThis: Clone gi-dellav/zerostack and benchmark it as a cheap parallel subagent runner alongside Claude Code.

items.title: larlarua/AutoCVE — Agent-driven automated CVE discovery platform for source code auditing, vulnerability verification, and report generation.
items.tldr: AutoCVE is an open-source agent-driven pipeline for automated CVE discovery, vulnerability verification, and report generation on source code.
items.whyItMatters: Could slot in as an unattended security-review stage before you review a finished PR in the morning.
items.tryThis: Clone larlarua/AutoCVE and add it as a pre-merge verification step alongside your test suite.

items.title: Javis603/token-monitor — Local-first desktop widget for tracking token usage, costs, and limits across 28+ AI coding tools—including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and OpenClaw—with multi-device sync.
items.tldr: token-monitor is a local desktop widget tracking token usage, cost, and rate limits across 28+ AI coding tools with multi-device sync.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you one place to see what overnight agent runs actually cost across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others before you scale up unattended usage.
items.tryThis: Install Javis603/token-monitor and cross-check its numbers against your provider billing dashboard for a week.

items.title: ongridio/ongrid — An ops AI Agent that understands your infrastructure, finds the root cause, and fixes it — right from Slack, Telegram, Lark or DingTalk.
items.tldr: Ongrid is an ops AI agent that diagnoses and fixes infrastructure issues triggered directly from Slack, Telegram, Lark or DingTalk.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete template for chat-triggered, event-driven agent runs you could adapt to kick off coding-agent tasks from your phone via chat.
items.tryThis: Look at ongrid's Slack/Telegram bot wiring as a template for triggering your own agents from chat.

items.title: Launch HN: Hoplite (YC S26) – Effortlessly deploy cloud coding agents
items.tldr: YC-backed Hoplite launches, porting your local Claude Code setup — sessions, memories, MCP servers — into cloud-hosted coding agents you can QA remotely.
items.whyItMatters: A ready-made path to trigger and check on agents from your phone instead of your desk, if the import of your existing setup actually holds up.
items.tryThis: Run Hoplite's onboarding import on one project and verify it carries over your MCP servers and skills intact.

clusters.title: Fable's prove-it-worked loop, made installable
clusters.summary: Both repos distill Claude Fable's completion/evidence/verification procedure into a reusable gate — one as a Claude Code plugin for Opus, the other as a portable skills-plus-eval package for any subagent.

clusters.title: Harness-agnostic control planes and proxies
clusters.summary: A wave of repos this cycle all solve the same problem: keep Claude Code (or Codex) as the front end while swapping, rotating, or routing the backend model per subagent or per quota.

clusters.title: Controlling agents away from the desk
clusters.summary: Chat-triggered ops fixes and cloud-hosted coding-agent imports both point at the same workflow: kick off or check on an agent run from your phone instead of your desk.
